predecessors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
predecessors.text: Mingrelia (Samegrelo) with Lechkhumi and Svaneti, as the Dadiani princes held it when Georgia split into 'three kingdoms and several principalities'

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the principality, 'abolished, by Russia in 1867' (annexation 4 January 1867); Niko I renounced his rights in 1868 and the state 'became a Russian district until 1917'

ledger.x: 1463: the Dadiani principality of Mingrelia appears when Georgia splits.

c. 1700-1705: Abkhazia takes the Ghalidzga-Enguri strip. Samurzakano page: 'in 1705 three brothers of the Abkhazian ruling family, surnamed Chachba' divided their land, 'the third, Murzaqan, the southern part (from the Ghalidzga to the R. Enguri)'. Whether it was Mingrelian before is a reading from Cliopatria…
1720s: Upper Svaneti becomes its own principality.
1727: the Poti-Anaklia coast leaves the Mingrelian shape (-660 km2).
1867: Russia abolishes the Principality of Mingrelia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Russia won; the Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) returned Poti, Anapa and Akhalkalaki to Turkey.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) has the Sultan recognize Russia's possession of 'Georgia (with Imeretia, Mingrelia, Guria)'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages.
